root_cause.text: The setting of TIF_SVE for SVE-formatted ptrace writes was incorrectly placed inside a block guarded by system_supports_sme(), so on systems without SME, TIF_SVE was not set, leaving the task's state inconsistent.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "When SVE is supported but SME is not supported, a ptrace write to the NT_ARM_SVE regset can place the tracee into an invalid state where (non-streaming) SVE register data is stored in FP_STATE_SVE format but TIF_SVE is clear. This bug was introduced ... where the setting of TIF_SVE was moved into a block which is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true." The patch removes the `if (system_supports_sme())` conditional, ensuring TIF_SVE is set regardless of SME support.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the system_supports_sme() guard to fix a bug where TIF_SVE was not set for SVE operations on systems without SME support.
intent_record.what: Removed the outer if (system_supports_sme()) check that previously guarded the switch statement, making the switch unconditional.
intent_record.how: Previously, the modification of target->thread.svcr and setting of TIF_SVE/TIF_SME flags only occurred when the system supports SME. Now, these operations are performed unconditionally in sve_set_common, ensuring that TIF_SVE is set even on systems without SME support.
